content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper tries to migrate the success of text to image into text to graph domain. Despite that there are many existing works on text conditional graph generation, this work claims that the major difference is to generate novel graphs, rather than explaining the text with graphs. Technically the graphs are first learned with representation in VQ space, with the help of VQVAE, and then a signal autoregressive language model is learned for text and VQ sequence of graph representation. Experiments on synthetic data and a wikipedia dataset show that the proposed method is able to generate better graphs compared to existing competitors.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
This paper is well presented in terms of the writing, and the method and paper is easy to follow. However there are several major issues with the current paper.

- There’s little or no novelty in terms of the technical treatment. The graph VAE with VQ and the autoregressive language models are all well studied by now, and the paper put these two together in a pipeline without much of the investigation of design choices, or the justifications of the current model designs. So technical contribution may not be the main focus of this paper. 

- The problem is not well motivated. I would focus more if the application or the problem proposed is interesting/important enough to cover the shortage of the technical novelty. However I’m not fully convinced by the applications as demonstrated in the experiments. The synthetic one is not connected to the potential applications, while the wikipedia one is also a bit unnatural where the graphs are post processed and it is not directly linked to any practical application. 

Actually I might have a better example where the authors could try. Say one can describe the desired property of a drug using text, and the model is responsible to generate the molecule graph given this text. This task should be difficult but if one can demonstrate good results on this, then that would be an important paper. I believe there are some preliminary studies in the domain, which I hope the authors could also explore/discuss more in this direction.

- Experimental section is also weak, where only small scaled experiments are done and only one baseline method is considered, given that many text/graph generative models are there.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is written clearly, and I think it is reproducible given the simplicity of the treatment. However I’m not convinced that the paper is novel or of high quality, due to the reasons I pointed out in the weakness section.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall this is an application paper that tries to sell the problem of text to graphs. However the application itself is not well motivated by the experiments, and the technical part is also somewhat straightforward without much depth in terms of the contribution.
content.correctness: 4: All of the claims and statements are well-supported and correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 1: The contributions are neither significant nor novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: In this paper, the authors deal with the problem of text-conditioned graph generation. They propose VQ-T2G, a model that consists of a discrete variational autoencoder that maps graphs into a discrete latent space and of a autoregressive transformer that learns a prior over the discrete space and text associated with graphs. The authors also introduce a synthetic and a real-world dataset for evaluating text-conditioned graph generation approaches. VQ-T2G outperforms a baseline model on both these datasets, while it also yields good performance on two datasets for unconditioned graph generation.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths

- The main strength of the paper lies in the novelty of the considered problem. This paper seems to be the first work that addresses the text-conditioned graph generation problem. I am pretty sure that more works will appear on this topic in the next few months and thus, this is a good starting point.

- The proposed method seems to perform relatively well on the two datasets. It captures graph properties better than Condgen in most cases. In the case of out-of-topic scores, it significantly outperforms Condgen.

Weaknesses

- Although the proposed model outperforms the baseline in the text-conditioned graph generation task, from the examples shown in Figure 2, it seems that the generated graphs are far from perfect even for very simple graphs such as the straight line graph. 

- The setting in the text-conditioned graph generation is a bit different from the setting in the text-conditioned image generation. In the latter, there are many different images that can match a given text caption. In the former setting, this is not generally true. For instance, the graphs in Figure 2 are uniquely defined by the given text. This questions the significance of the proposed method since graphs that perfectly match the given text can be generated using rule-based methods.

- One of my main concerns with this paper is that even though the proposed problem is interesting, its practical value is limited. I suggest the authors explain in more details why this problem is important and also provide potential real-world applications.

- I am not sure about the quality of the Wiki ego dataset. The authors assume that articles that have similar titles and first sentences also have structurally similar ego networks. But is this always the case? Do ego networks of different nodes share common subgraphs? 

- Condgen generates graphs conditioned on a feature vector and this vector is set equal to the byte-pair encoded text description for the graph. Since Condgen's performance critically depends on this vector, wouldn't it make more sense to use some pre-trained model such as BERT to produce the vector? 

- In subsection 5.2.2, the results of Table 2 are not discussed in the paper.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity: The paper is generally well written and organized.\
Novelty: As already discussed the considered task is new. This is also the main strength of the paper in my view. On the other hand, the proposed method is a well-known approach adapted to the setting of text-conditioned graph generation.\
Quality: The quality of the paper is good, though not supported by very comprehensive experiments.\
Reproducibility: The paper provides enough information to reproduce the reported results.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall, this is an interesting paper which introduces a novel problem inspired by recent advances in multimodal modelling in computer vision. The proposed model combines some existing methods, but can well serve as a starting point for this task. I really liked the paper, the quality is good, but I have some concerns with regards to the practical value of the task/method. In my view, it is unlikely that practitioners will use the ideas presented in the paper. I suggest the authors list some real-world applications of the considered problem and also empirically evaluate the model on at least one of them.
content.correctness: 4: All of the claims and statements are well-supported and correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper:
This paper suggests VQ-T2G, a method for generating graphs based on a natural language prompt that heavily relies on VQ-VAE.  
They tested their model on two datasets Wiki-ego and a synthetic one.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
**Strengths**
- The paper is well-written and clear. 
- This is a relatively novel problem to tackle. 

**Weaknesses**
- There isn't enough discussion on how and why graph generation from text is an important task.
- It's mentioned in 5.2.3 that Condgen wasn't designed for text conditioning. So, the comparison in table 1., especially the off-topic column, sounds a little unfair.
- Why do the authors think that VQ-T2G is outperforming other baselines on Wigi ego but not the two-community dataset (table 2)?
- Since there aren't a lot of baselines to compare with, I think that there should be a proper time/memory complexity analysis between VQ-T2G and Condgen. 
- Mostly a suggestion: have authors created a small subset of building blocks of the graphs with their corresponding text and done pre-training/finetuning on them? e.g. straight line, loop and etc. 
- Dall-E doesn't have a good understanding of geometry and numbers. It can generate a very realistic strawberry image but if you ask for "a picture with 5 strawberries" the chances are high that you don't get the picture with the correct number of strawberries. What was your observation in your case?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The paper is clear and well-written. \
The problem they are trying to tackle is relatively novel but the method's novelty is limited. \
I encourage the authors to release their synthetic dataset and their method source code for the sake of reproducibility.
content.summary_of_the_review:
Most of the points are mentioned in the strengths and weaknesses section but in summary, generating graphs from text is a new problem that I believe there aren't (many) prior studies on it.
However, the authors should have a bit more discussion on why this is an important task, have a more thorough comparison with the baseline, and do more ablation studies on their method.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

content.summary_of_the_paper: In this paper, the authors propose to tackle the generation of graphs conditioned on text. In doing so, the authors proposed to use a quantized auto-encoder of graphs (with adjacency matrix and node features) where the decoder is also conditioned on the text tokens. Sone quantitative experiments and visualizations are used to show the performance of the proposed method.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
This paper tackles an interesting, novel problem. The problem of conditional generation of graphs is one that is relatively unexplored.

However the methodology and experiments in the current draft pose several issues that should be addressed before appearing in this venue:

1. The description of the method is pretty unclear. A more concrete description would then allow an interested reader to reproduce the proposed method.

2. The experiment is not properly designed. The setup of the only baseline to compare with in the conditional generation, namely CondGen, is not clear. Furthermore  the result of unconditional graph generation should be done with more baselines (to name a few, NetGAN, GraphRNN, the later of which is pretty strong one) and preferably on more real-world datasets (to name a few, datasets proposed in Dobson, P. and Doig, A. Distinguishing enzyme structures
from non-enzymes without alignments / Sen, P., Namata, G., Bilgic, M., Getoor, L., Galligher, B.,
and Eliassi-Rad, T. Collective classification in network)

3. Since this is a new problem, some ablation study for the complexity of this problem, like the distribution of graphs' properties, may be helpful for readers. This unfortunately is not present.

4. As a result of all of the above, it becomes hard to assess the potential of this work given its current form.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: This paper should have more clarity for the reader to reproduce the work, has novelty in problem, and may have only limited contributions.
content.summary_of_the_review: Based on the strengths and weaknesses, I would recommend a rejection of this paper.
